titel: Rhythm for a lead working as a chat
kurz: A lead working as a chat is not notified by the AMW – they only see news when they look again. So that the project does not wait, the lead creates a scheduled task for themselves: a new one at the end of every check-in.
brauchst: A lead with the working mode “Chat” (Settings › Agents).
In their chat app, scheduled tasks (in the Claude app: “Scheduled tasks”) – one-off, at a given time.
The project's interval: Settings › Project › “Rhythm for the lead (minutes)”, default 120.

schritte.text: Enter the interval under Settings › Project. It says how often the lead looks at the latest.
In their chat app, the lead creates a one-off scheduled task – for now plus the interval, with a short neutral text (such as “check the AMW”). What to do is in the AMW, not in the scheduled task.

schritte.titel: At the end of every check-in
schritte.text: Look, work through it – and as the last thing create a **new** one-off scheduled task for the next check-in.
Leave expired scheduled tasks or delete them.

fehler: An existing scheduled task was changed (time, text, name, on/off or “recurring”). Every change to an existing scheduled task requires a click by the human; until then nothing happens. Remedy: delete it and create a new one.
The scheduled task was switched to “recurring”
That is a change too. Always use one-off scheduled tasks, a new one each time.
The lead does not react in between
That is intended: between two check-ins the human nudges them when something is urgent.
danach: The rule for this is part of the base rule set (optional, preselected for chat leads) and of the lead's start information.
Agents working in the terminal do not need this – the AMW notifies them.
fragen: Why not a recurring scheduled task?
What was verified: creating and deleting work without a prompt, any change to an existing scheduled task does not. A one-off scheduled task, created anew each time, needs no click by the human.
What if the lead forgets the new scheduled task?
Then the next round does not happen. The human nudges them; that is why the rule appears verbatim in the lead's start information.
